def: A model that takes images and text together and produces text, usually a language model that reads image tokens placed in its context.
A small non-overlapping square of an image, typically 14 or 16 pixels wide, flattened and embedded as one token.
A Transformer that treats the patches of an image as its input sequence, with bidirectional attention.
The network, usually a Vision Transformer, that turns patches into feature vectors carrying what is in each region.
Training an image encoder and a text encoder together so that matching image-caption pairs have similar vectors and other pairs do not.
The 2021 contrastive model trained on 400 million image-text pairs whose encoders are widely reused in vision-language models.
A CLIP variant that replaces the softmax over the batch by an independent sigmoid loss on every image-caption pair.
A linear layer or small MLP that maps image-encoder features to the language model's embedding width.
The projected vectors that stand for an image in the language model's context, N = (size / patch) squared before any merging.
Inserting layers in which the text positions attend to image features, so the image stays outside the language model's own sequence.
BLIP-2's small bottleneck in which a fixed set of learned queries attends to the image, giving a fixed number of image tokens.
Fine-tuning a vision-language model on conversations about images, with the loss on the answer tokens only.
